This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 02-07-2022 at about 12.15 p.m., the petitioner was riding his TVS XL moped bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JD-6036, near Kunigal Junction, Tumakuru, carefully and cautiously.

When he reached near Kunigal Junction, at that time all of a sudden a TATA ACE vehicle, bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091, being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, with high speed, neglecting all the traffic rules and regulations, came from Bengaluru side towards Gubbi side on the ring road and Raju S.M vs Future Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110073581/
2 dashed against the TVS XL Moped of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Due to the said impact, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Tumakuru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient and underwent surgery.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Tumakuru Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the TATA ACE bearing No.KA-06-AA-9091 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.3 is the insurer and respondent No.4 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1, 3 and 4 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear in the case and hence he is placed as ex-parte.
Thereafter, as per the order dated 20-12-2023, the respondents No.1 and 2 are deleted.
4. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.VGC0787556000100 in respect of TATA ACE bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the driver and rider of the vehicles involved in the accident were possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive their respective vehicles.
The petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
No accident taken place as stated in the claim petition.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE bearing No.KA-06-9091 and said vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself and there is no nexus between the injuries sustained to the petitioner and he has filed false petition to get unlawful gain.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the TATA ACE bearing No.KA-06-9091 was not possessing valid fitness certificate and permit to ply the said vehicle on the road.
As such there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and rules and regulations of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.4, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.4 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
He has contended that, at the time of accident he was holding valid and effective driving licence bearing No.KA0620190011459 to drive his TATA ACE bearing No.KA-06-9091.
He was proceeding from Bengaluru to Gubbi with a load of vegetable and was driving his vehicle by obeying the traffic rules and in complete control.
The petitioner without following any traffic rules all of sudden entered to the middle of the road from the left side most corner of the road to the center of the road, in rash and negligent manner.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7 and 15, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 and dashing the same to TVS XL moped bearing Reg. No.KA-04-JD-6036 of the petitioner.
Further it reveals that, due to said impact the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his chest, right leg and face.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.7 that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

13. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06- AA-9091 in the alleged accident,
issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.4 in respect of said Tata Ace bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-AA-9091 and its validity as on the date of accident are not in dispute.

The respondent No.3 & 4 have specifically denied that, the above stated facts and circumstances of the accident and have taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, as the petitioner without following the traffic rules all of sudden entered the road and came to the center of the road from the left side most corner of the road, in a rash and negligent manner and due to which even after applicability of brakes and enormous efforts made by the respondent No.4 to avoid the accident, he could not avoid the accident.

Though the respondent No.3 & 4 have specifically contended that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself, they have failed to establish the same.
The respondent No.4 has not stepped into witness box to depose the contentions taken in his written statement on oath.

Further,
except the self serving statements of the R.W.1, who is representative/Administrative officer of the respondent No.3 company, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.3 to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the moped by the petitioner.

Though the learned counsel for respondents No.3 and 4 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to his own negligence or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
Further, the petitioner/P.W.1 has unequivocally denied all the suggestions made in his cross-examination.

Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazer and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident on the middle of 80 feet wide road, at Kunigal Junction, Tumakuru Town, due to dashing of offending Tata Ace vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 to the TVS Excel moped bearing No.KA- 04-JD-6036 of the petitioner, who was proceeding from Goluru towards Tumakuru.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident has not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the given facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg.
No.KA-06-AA-9091.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091.

the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 and he has sustained grievous injuries.

As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained fracture of right side 1st to 5th ribs, left side 1st and 2nd ribs, right clavicle fracture undisplaced, right lateral malleolus fracture + chronic SDH and right zygomatic fracture and for the said injuries he has taken conservative treatment.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e.
pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1973.
The accident has taken place on 02-07-2022 at about 12.15 P.M. Therefore, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 50 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of right side 1st to 5th ribs, left side 1st and 2nd ribs, right clavicle fracture undisplaced, right lateral malleolus fracture + chronic SDH and right zygomatic fracture and for the said injuries he has taken conservative treatment.

Further he has Raju S.M vs Future Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110073581/
7 deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of 22% to the right lower limb, 24% to the right upper limb and 18% to the whole body.

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross- examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further,
he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, there is no disability to the petitioner and without following the guidelines issued in the Gazette notification of the Central Government he has assessed his disability and in order to held the petitioner to claim compensation he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 02-07-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 30-07-2024, which is after lapse of two years from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further, he has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the petitioner has taken conservative treatment and not undergone any surgery.
Further he has admitted that, all the injuries sustained by the petitioner are healed and except right clavicle fracture which is mal-united, all other fractures are united.
Further it is pertinent to note that, as per the guidelines issued by the Central Government for the assessment of disability, the clavicle bone fracture does not carry any disability.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as coolie and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-.
b)

As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 50 years is 13.

21. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.3 is the insurer and respondent No.4 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy issued by the respondent No.3, in respect to offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091, the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Further, the copy of driving licence bearing No.KA0620190011459 available on record, clearly goes to show that, at the time of accident the respondent No.4 was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.

The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-06-AA- 9091 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.4 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.4.
Therefore, the respondent No.3 and 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,71,102/- from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Tumakuru Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the TATA ACE bearing No.KA-06-AA-9091 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.3 is the insurer and respondent No.4 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It has contended that, the driver and rider of the vehicles involved in the accident were possessing valid and effective driving licence to drive their respective vehicles.
The petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
No accident taken place as stated in the claim petition.
There is no negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA ACE bearing No.KA-06-9091 and said vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself and there is no nexus between the injuries sustained to the petitioner and he has filed false petition to get unlawful gain.
As such there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy and rules and regulations of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 02-07- 2022 at about 12.15 p.m., near Kunigal Junction, Tumkuru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the TATA ACE vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

No.KA-06-AA-9091.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.3 & 4 have specifically denied that, the above stated facts and circumstances of the accident and have taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, as the petitioner without following the traffic rules all of sudden entered the road and came to the center of the road from the left side most corner of the road, in a rash and negligent manner and due to which even after applicability of brakes and enormous efforts made by the respondent No.4 to avoid the accident, he could not avoid the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091 and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the given facts and circumstances of the case it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents and even nothing has been elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is absolutely no material on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No.KA-06-AA-9091.

Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
Further it is pertinent to note that, as per the guidelines issued by the Central Government for the assessment of disability, the clavicle bone fracture does not carry any disability.
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained by him, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as coolie and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident has taken place in the year 2022.
The evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tata Ace bearing Reg. No. KA-06-AA- 9091 the accident in question has occurred and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.4.
